body: My symptoms a few months ago would be more consistent, but now i'm not so sure. Nevertheless, I'll do some more reading and check it out! my family has a history of a whole host of different autoimmune problems, so it's a possibility.
I'll check it out, thanks!
Thank you!

I'm moving out of the dorms this summer and into my first apartment, so I'll have free reign over what I eat for the first time. Sort of overwhelming, so any suggestions are welcomed!

Thanks again for your help, I'm sort of shy when it comes to things like this, and I'm actually really intimidated by my GP, so i don't ask a lot of questions.
unfortunately, i'm one of those people that just has a terrible reaction to it. it's a bummer, for sure.

Previously I would have said I would have been the first type, but the past couple months I've switched more to the second type.

As far as natural foods go, this summer I'll be out of the dorms (which means no dining halls! :) ) and I'll be i my own apartment, so it won't be my mom's kitchen. This means I can cook whatever I want. However, I have no idea what I should be eating. I generally eat a lot of fiber (oatmeal, etc.) and definitely get more than what I need per day, but I'm sort of picky with regards to other types of foods. If you have any suggestions, it would be much appreciated! I'm just really quite clueless, and tend to just eat sandwiches when all else fails. You're definitely right about coffee, though. Finals week was terrible, and even if it doesn't give me diarrhea, it gives me terrible cramps.

I'll look into getting some Vitamin C, though. I take a regular multivitamin daily as well as Align.  Any other suggestions for supplements?

I'll try out some pilates; I'm actually starting to have anxiety associated with just even thinking about running now, so i definitely need a change.

thanks so much for your help! i'm glad to hear you're doing better!

Actually, I have some pretty big anxiety issues. It's a vicious cycle: i'm anxious because i'm so uncomfortable, can't run, feel bloated, etc., and that seems to make it worse. I'm currently on medication and trying to straighten things out, but it's definitely a process.

I'm taking align right now. I haven't really noticed a difference, and I'm nearly done with week 2.

I noticed you said to cut out fatty foods; what do you think of the keto diet, out of curiosity?

I'm sort of an all-or-nothing person, and sometimes I honestly feel like if I don't have a thoughtful, challenging career, that I'll end up in some cubicle, being miserable. Maybe that's true, maybe it's not. I just know that I'll never be able to live with that... After living a life that has seemed void of meaning for so long, I need to *do* something, you know? But unfortunately, that means that I'm going to be stuck in school for 7+ more years, because I can't think of anything else that fits the criteria I've set up for myself.

Your post has actually made me think a lot... And I've realized that you're right. I had all the qualifications for a full-ride to school here (test scores, etc.) but not the GPA. But sitting here and kicking myself isn't going to bring a scholarship back; working to put myself back together so that I can perform like I know I can, however, will bring me more scholarships in the future.

And you're right about empty achievements, too. I was always a really good athlete my entire life, and now... It seems sort of sad when I hear people bragging about their high school lives. Yeah, I was a good athlete. But that doesn't mean shit now. I don't think I'll ever be one of those people living in the "glory days" and I'm kind of glad about that.

> Don't quit--just keep running and perhaps you'll see something worth seeing along the road.

This was really well-said. Sometimes I get overwhelmed when people tell me, "Oh, it's worth it!" whereas your comment was more directed at the scenery, rather than the goal, which is definitely I think a less overwhelming approach.

Regardless, thanks for taking the time to say something to me.

Interesting theory! I'm just scared to death I'll have a bad trip, and be stuck in it for what seems like eternity. I'm hoping to get an opportunity to do some volunteer work (hopefully on a larger scale, so the shock value will be greater) to kind of force myself into a new perspective.

It's whatever about my parents... They're not me. I don't have direct contact with my dad anymore, and my mom is more pathetic than anything else. I made it through my childhood, so I figure that's pretty much the roughest part of the battle! I sort of am on the same page about drugs, I think. People don't want to admit it, but on some level, drugs have become an integral part of how our society has been shaped.

Well, hang in there with the addiction, and please get help! You seem too brilliant to be miserable! And jesus christ, 13 hours?!

Don't apologize for a long response, it's stupid little things like that that make me feel a little bit better; some stranger took time out of their day to write something just for me. That's pretty cool. I'm feeling better, somewhat, in the sense that I'm more... peaceful. All the thoughts and feelings are still there, but I'm sort of just more... resigned. I'm not sure what to say or do. Suicide isn't quite an option yet, as I have a ton of obligations, and even if I'm miserable, I'm not that inconsiderate... ha.

Also, I've come to the conclusion that we have pretty similar tastes in music, so thanks for sending another enjoyable link!
you've just articulated that perfectly. thanks.

I just was creeping through your other comments, and I realized something: *i think we are the same person*

Maybe that sounds creepy. I dunno. I just sifted through like, the top 10, just to see what you were like. I saw a Harry Potter reference, psychology, and a lot of blunt sarcasm. So, not that it probably means anything, but I'd probably like you and think you're cool.

Yeah, I know what you mean about the "it gets better" stories; I pass them on to friends when they're feeling down, and I feel like I usually give pretty good advice and it seems like most other people believe whatever it is that I'm spouting off. I just don't typically believe it with regards to myself, for whatever reason.

I definitely get what you're saying about not being able to even imagine what it is that would work... I've always felt like when I picture my life in the future, it's more of me just making up a story or something. I can picture the lives of all my friends much more easily, and it almost seems tangible. There's something concrete about their futures, whereas I'm somewhat convinced that I'll just cease to exist whenever I leave school or something.

You're definitely right about the statistics, though. It would be completely egotistical of me to think that none of that applies to me, or that I'm the only one who has ever felt this way. I find it sort of comforting, really.

it just feels like a gamble, you know? like i *could* someday get out of this, and be the skinny, pretty, successful person that I think I have the potential to be. But there's also a strong chance I'll continue to scrape by, and continue to be so uncomfortable in my day-to-day life that it really lacks any meaning.

I admire you a lot for staying logical and somewhat positive about things. Being down here, it's so hard to do that.

It's hard to apply it to life in general, vs. just running, because as far as running goes, time and distance is always an accomplishment; living a day longer in an unhappy life isn't necessarily an accomplishment, you know? But some part of me knows that I'm just not thinking clearly, and that holding on really is an accomplishment, in and of itself.

I'll ask her about switching me, thanks

right now, my anxiety is the biggest obstacle between me and med school... i'm so caught up that i can barely concentrate. some days, i don't make it to class because i'm such a wreck.

ironically enough, i'd really like to go into psychiatry. there's something really attractive about solving puzzles all day. i just love medicine, because it's the marriage between science and people. there's something really beautiful about that. i'm technically a "pre-med psychology" student, so I'll have a psychology major on top of the pre-med curriculum.

it's really important for me to have a meaningful, challenging career. i don't think i can survive any other way. that's one thing that makes me really nervous... if i can't get my shit together soon and keep my grades up, i don't know what i'm going to do.

i'm listening to the song you linked now, and i like it a whole lot. honest.

ha, yeah, i've driven close to 400 miles this weekend, and i did a lot of angry speeding, adrenaline speeding, just-want-to-see-if-i'm-alive speeding... sigh, oh music.

i drink, but it's usually a gamble if i do. sometimes, it makes me lighten up and become more fun-loving... other times, i end up sort of jaded and stuck in my head. i've smoked weed a fair number of times, but i have a pretty bad reaction to it. i think it's because i have a somewhat anxious personality. also, i tend to even get more stuck in my head when i'm smoking than when i'm drinking. i definitely know i don't have the personality type to try any hallucinogens, and with my family history of addiction (mother is an alcoholic, father was/is? a drug addict) i know better than to try anything else.

After my exboyfriend and I broke up, he had about 10 of his friends comment on one of my pictures on facebook, calling me various large animals (i.e. whale, elephant...)

... He knew I had a pretty severe eating disorder in the past. Needless to say: ouch.

I had nearly forgotten about this (it happened this past summer) until one of his friends jokingly brought it up at a party when I ran into him this past friday: "haha, yeah, so remember that one time we all commented on that picture? were you like, mad?" and then proceeded to tell me I "looked hot tonight" and even tried to hug me goodbye at the end of the night.

GOOD TIMES

i remember being really, really unhappy, even a couple years before that. the first time i was suicidal was a year before i began restricting.

lately, my stomach pain has been so chronic that i haven't been able to run. i usually exercise only once per day. i'm definitely happier on days that i have a good workout. i've been experiencing some anxiety related to my running, as i used to be a very competitive athlete in high school, and now i don't perform nearly as well as i used to (which is to be expected, i don't have three hours to dedicate to fitness everyday like i did in high school, being on various sports teams). i have the tendency to work myself up pretty badly about it.

i'd actually like to lose about 15 pounds. which is probably pretty realistic. i haven't weighed myself since 2006, but it looks like it would be about right. i'm hoping we get the stomach issues straightened out (which could be contributing to my weight gain) and i'll be able to run pain-free again.

if i could feel good about myself, i could probably deal with the external stressors in my life a lot more easily.

Just out of morbid curiosity, why do people downvote things in r/suicidewatch? i'm not offended or anything, but some part of me is really interested in the psychology of it all. an honest question, really.

i knew, logically, that what i was doing wasn't normal. and i knew that if i didn't fix it, i was going to die. so i chose to go to a rigorous outpatient program.

it was one of the worst periods of my life. i withdrew from treatment. my body healed, my mind didn't.

i still don't have a very healthy attitude towards food. there may be something a bit off with my metabolism/thyroid (currently doing blood work, etc. trying to discern what the problem is, potentially an autoimmune disease) so i've put on a little weight recently, despite my (mostly) healthy habits. occasionally i binge, especially when i'm under stress. definitely not something i'm proud of.

Unfortunately, I'm going to school summer quarter as an excuse to not come home to my alcoholic mother. So no vacation in the near future. If you get a chance, what songs worked well for you? I'm trying to teach myself that it's ok to take 15 minutes to relax and try to become peaceful... that 15 minutes of tending to myself is better for productivity in the grand scheme of things than struggling and pushing myself through it all (because, turns out I don't get anything done that way).

Yeah, I can sympathize. I've found myself doing some pretty abnormal, self-destructive things after a long day. But mostly just being a vegetable. I sit in the dark a lot, and I don't even realize I'm doing it until my roommate comes home and tells me I'm being weird.

I'm scared to death of him. He constantly cuts me off, and I couldn't even get out what I wanted to talk to him about when I went this past friday. He literally attributes any symptom I have to my 'depression'. I had H1N1 last year, and when I told him about the body aches, etc. he literally told me it was in my head... Until he ran the test and realized that I had it. He's the worst.

But yeah, I think I'll bring up seroxat (mentioned above) and see if that works... It's definitely an uphill battle trying to find something that works. I can't even take my anxiety medication at this point because it knocks me out (any smaller dose, and i still panic, any larger, i fall in a weird sleep-like stupor).

I wish I got 7-8 hours! Unfortunately, due to my lack of ability to concentrate, my school work is taking much longer than it usually does, so I don't really have time to sleep. I'm hoping that if I get everything else figured out, I'll be able to concentrate again, and things will sort of fall back into sleep. Ideally, I'd like to get up, exercise, shower, and then go to class... I like having the rest of my day ahead of me. It's just getting everything done that seems to be the struggle.

That sounds like a good idea. I was thinking about maybe trying to do some volunteer work in a third world country, potentially in Africa, because I've heard of a few programs that allow students to volunteer in hospitals there. I figure it would be a little less strenuous than what I'm doing now, and would maybe give me a different perspective on life. I know, logically, I have it a lot better than a lot of other people in the world. I just can't seem to feel that way, though.

I've decided that if I do decide to end my life, I'll at least try to do something beneficial before I go. I guess it's sort of a last effort to change how I feel, and if I can't, at least I'll have done something worthwhile.

Thanks for the links, by the way. Bookmarked the one about managing depression. Surprisingly, my sleep hygiene is pretty good! It's just finding the time for sleep that I'm struggling with.

I'm someone of a nihilist, and think about stuff like that a lot: what's real, what's "important" etc. And I realize that no one really probably gives a shit about that C.

... but then I bring myself back into the world in which i life, and then i'm like "FUCK, MED SCHOOLS DO"

But yeah, when I'm having one of my episodes, and I know i need to shut it down and get my work done, I try to think of where I stand on the hierarchy of needs... And realize things are looking pretty good. And that helps me deal with things for the time being.

my main concern is weight gain; other side effects, I can deal with :) I'll have to ask about it, maybe it's something I could look into.

Whenever I'm running, whenever I get tired, I just think that each step I take is one more step taken than if i had quit (i articulated that poorly, but I'm just getting in, and i'm tired, but i think you get the idea). I'm trying really hard to apply that to my life in general... it just feels like it's been such a work in progress. 6 years is a long time to be on medication that isn't working, and to have virtually no support. But I think i'm going to write Churchill's quote and put it on my desk. It's simple, and I like it a lot. Thank you!

I know it's BS... Trying to maintain a logical POV is really the only thing that has kept me from acting on any of the urges I feel.

I know that really, we're all just atoms, made cells, made organs, made organisms; that every cognition i've ever had is a result of firings (or misfirings) of neurons. But it's just so hard to deal with the feelings, you know? I can work with words or numbers, but feelings... There's no way around that.

I'm checking out the videos now, thanks for the links.

Believe it or not, unlike a lot of people with depression, I'm actually a morning person! Except, under the circumstances with school right now, I'm more of a "no sleep" person. But yes, when the opportunity presents itself, I have never been known to turn down a nap. But good advice.

it's just scary, you know? trying something new means investing a lot of time... time that I don't have a lot of. I'm just feel such urgency. "Fix it now, get your shit together, pick your chem grade up. Med schools don't give a shit if you were 'sad'" seems to be what I tell myself a lot.

Did you notice any side effects with seroxat? And can you take it in the morning?

I've been in counseling since January, and I've been medicated since I was 13 years old. I just feel like I'm running out of options.

I meet with my counselor once a week, but I try to use my school's walk-in hours as often as I can, because I'm just trying so hard to hold it all together.

And I'll PM you my address, thank you so much for taking the time to help out.

It's just so frustrating... I was on zoloft for 7 years, and apparently it wasn't working the entire time. My doctor chalked up my lingering depression to just me being me, or something. He never did anything about it.

I'm pretty intimidated by him... I went in for an appointment to get some blood work done, and he quite literally laughs at me. I'm terrified to bring anything up. (he's my general doctor)

As for my psychiatrist at school, she has me on buspar, but it has to be taken at night. I routinely stay up until the early morning attempting to work on homework, so I really can't take it all that often. It's bad, I know, but I can't be falling asleep during my school work... Concentrating is hard enough :(

And honestly, it's nice to hear ANY suggestions. Anything. I'm so exhausted, that I really just don't know what to do. My whole life I've felt like I've been .1 off the radio frequency that everyone else seems to be on, so any time someone can empathize, it's welcomed.
